newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Mexico's Mastretta wins prestigious literary prize.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Mastretta wins prestigious literary prize.

text.p: Mexican writer Angeles Mastretta won on Friday Venezuela's Romulo Gallegos prize for fiction, one of the Spanish language's most prestigious literary awards, with her romance "Mal de Amor", or "Love Sick".

The 48-year old journalist and poet beat six other finalists to the $60,000 prize, including Argentine novelist Tomas Eloy Martinez's best-selling investigation of the myth of Evita Peron "Santa Evita".

"'Mal de Amor' is a very good novel, the best of the lot," said Brazilian journalist and judge Bella Jozef. The panel of five judges praised the 375-page novel's lyrical and imaginative reading of Mexican history as seen through the daily lives and loves of a small family.

Previous winners of the prize, awarded every two years, include nobel-prize winning Colombian author Gabriel Garcia Marquez for "One Hundred Years of Solitude" in 1972 and Peruvian writer Maria Vargas Llosa for "The Green Mansion" in 1967.
